newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Santos workers decide to continue striking.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Santos workers decide to continue striking.

text.p: Administrative portworkers at the key Brazilian port of Santos have decided to continue their strike for at least another day and new talks with the port authority will be needed to solve the dispute, a spokesman said.

"The strike continues," he said. Fresh talks with port authority CODESP were scheduled for 0900 local/1200 GMT Wednesday and the union would later hold an assembly at 2000 local to decide whether to continue the strike, he added.

The portworkers halted work earlier on Tuesday in protest against not being consulted about a switch to 24-hour operations at the port. They said they would need to renegotiate their collective wage agreement to take account of new shifts.
CODESP has proposed maintaining the existing wage agreement for six months while excluding all clauses related to shifts and working hours.

The port authority has also requested extra workers registered with the OGM, a central organ which regulates the port's employees. These would mainly be seasonal workers employed during the sugar harvest, a CODESP spokeswoman said.
If the OGM agrees to release these workers, the port could function normally despite the strike, she added. The organ was not expected to reach a decision before tomorrow.
